headline: President Bush assigned certain reports that the law requires the President to send Congress to other officials in the executive branch.
what_it_does: This order hands off, or delegates, some duties to send reports to Congress. Those duties had belonged to the President, and the order gives them to other officials in the executive branch. Only the title was available, so the exact reports and officials involved are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: Heads of federal agencies and departments
who_it_affects.how: Some of them became responsible for preparing and sending certain required reports to Congress in place of the President.

who_it_affects.group: Members of Congress and their committees
who_it_affects.how: Some reports they receive may come from agency officials rather than directly from the President.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed July 31, 2003; the exact effective date is not stated in the provided material.
